request_summary: Dr. Michael Ortiz, MD (Summit Family Medicine) requests a routine MRI lumbar spine without contrast (72148) to evaluate a structural cause of persistent radiculopathy.

MRI-LUMBAR-001: No absolute contraindication to MRI documented in the record. None is documented, although the note does not state that screening was done.
unmet_criteria: MRI-LUMBAR-001 conservative treatment (PT and/or NSAIDs/analgesics for at least 6 weeks): not documented. The submission states that no PT, medication trial or other conservative management was provided. This is missing documentation, not a documented treatment failure or refusal.
MRI-LUMBAR-001 red-flag pathway: not applicable. Red flags are documented as absent, so the conservative-treatment requirement is not waived.
reviewer_focus_areas: Was at least 6 weeks of conservative treatment (PT, NSAIDs/analgesics) actually tried? A request for records is appropriate before any adverse determination.
Does the worsening over the past 2 weeks involve any new neurological deficit that would change the red-flag assessment?
Confirm there is no MRI contraindication (implant, severe claustrophobia).
citations: MRI-LUMBAR-001: Low back pain with radiculopathy or neurological symptoms present for at least 6 weeks.

MRI-LUMBAR-001: OR red-flag symptoms present (cauda equina syndrome, progressive neurological deficit, suspected malignancy or infection, significant trauma) — conservative treatment is not required in this case.
MRI-LUMBAR-001: Conservative treatment (physical therapy and/or NSAIDs/analgesics) attempted for at least 6 weeks, unless red flags above are present.
MRI-LUMBAR-001: No absolute contraindication to MRI (e.g., non-MRI-compatible implant, severe claustrophobia without sedation plan) documented in the record.
rationale: Symptom duration is documented and no red flags are present, so conservative treatment is required.
